$meta.title: Three exposure measures, side by side and never combined

measures.definition: Mean ONS (2019) probability of automation, weighted by residents' occupations
measures.notes_common_to_every_row: central value, with the lower and upper bounds from the occupation crosswalk

measures.definition: Mean DfE (2023) AI occupational exposure score, all AI, standardised
measures.notes_common_to_every_row: central value, with the lower and upper bounds from the occupation crosswalk

measures.definition: Share of employed residents in occupations at GLA (2026) generative AI exposure levels 1 to 4
measures.notes_common_to_every_row: central value, with the lower and upper bounds from the occupation crosswalk

$meta.publisher: Office for National Statistics; Department for Education; GLA Economics
$meta.table: ONS (2019) probability of automation, Table 9; DfE (2023) AI occupational exposure, Annex 1 Table 1; GLA Economics (2026) Working Paper 103, Table A5.1; Census 2021 occupation
$meta.edition: measures of 2019, 2023 and 2026 applied to Census 2021 occupations
$meta.citation: Workstream C automation.csv, from ONS (2019), DfE (2023) and GLA Economics (2026)
$meta.vintage: Census 2021 occupations (lockdown); scores carried across classifications
$meta.caveat: Exposure is technical potential, not forecast job loss. The three measures answer different questions and are not combined. The ONS high risk share for Burnley is not quoted: the published cell is suppressed.
$meta.next_release: when any of the three measures is revised
$meta.rules: No company or person is named. No estimate is shown as fact. Derived figures carry their arithmetic.
